model.name: Qwen2.5-0.5B
model.positions: RoPE on queries and keys, pairs (i, i + 32); YaRN rescales the frequencies

examples.title: Pass key · 8K tokens
examples.prompt:
8,192 tokens, pass key 10 % in: There is an important info hidden inside a lot of irrelevant text. Find it and memorize them. I will quiz you about the important information there.
[The grass is green.… 3,047 characters]
The pass key is 21452. Remember it. 21452 is the pass key.
[… 27,421 characters]
What is the pass key? The pass key is

capture.attention: torch scaled_dot_product_attention in chunks of 1,024 query rows, layer by layer

settings.rope: the model’s config.json, no rope_scaling (RoPE base 10⁶, trained to 32,768)
settings.yarn: rope_scaling as Qwen documents it, through transformers’ Qwen2RotaryEmbedding
settings.yarn-flat: the same with attention_factor 1.0 (no temperature); book only

passkeyPrompt.task: There is an important info hidden inside a lot of irrelevant text. Find it and memorize them. I will quiz you about the important information there.
passkeyPrompt.garbage: The grass is green. The sky is blue. The sun is yellow. Here we go. There and back again.
passkeyPrompt.info: The pass key is {key}. Remember it. {key} is the pass key.
passkeyPrompt.question: What is the pass key? The pass key is
passkeyPrompt.source: Mohtashami & Jaggi, Landmark Attention (arXiv 2305.16300), run_test.py; lines joined with newlines, garbage cut to a number of characters, pass key random in 1 … 50,000 (seeded per length and depth)

capture.decoding: greedy, with the loop’s own KV cache

book.source: Arthur Conan Doyle, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes (1892), Project Gutenberg eBook #1661, public domain
book.cut: the text between the Project Gutenberg START and END markers, stripped
book.start: To Sherlock Holmes she is always

capture.cols: token 0, the pass-key sentence up to its first full stop, the key’s digits where the sentence repeats them, and the rows (masses and strips use every key)
capture.x: input to attention after input_layernorm, first 64 of 896, at the rows
capture.out: o_proj output at the rows, first 64 of 896

extras.rows: [R] prompt position of each shown query row (the tokens)
extras.cols: [K] prompt position of each shown key column (the keyTokens)
extras.layer.*: the YaRN run at depth 0.1, shown rows × shown columns; the weights are the softmax over every key, so a row of shown weights sums to less than 1
extras.rope.layer.*.scores: [H, R, K] the same prompt with the model’s own RoPE
extras.rope.layer.*.weights: [H, R, K] the same prompt with the model’s own RoPE
extras.<setting>.mass.info: [L, H] attention of the last prompt token on the pass-key sentence
extras.<setting>.mass.key: [L, H] attention of the last prompt token on the pass key’s digits
extras.<setting>.mass.first: [L, H] attention of the last prompt token on token 0
extras.<setting>.entropy: [L, H] entropy (nats) of the last prompt token’s attention over all keys
extras.<setting>.strip: [L, H, 128] the last prompt token’s attention summed over 128 equal bins of positions
extras.ramp: [32] YaRN’s ramp γ_i: 0 keeps θ_i, 1 divides it by the factor
extras.book.edges: [257] position bins of the book loss
extras.book.<setting>: [256] mean next-token loss (nats) per bin, rope / yarn / yarn-flat
extras.passkey.correct: [2, lengths, depths] 1 where greedy decoding gave the pass key; rope, then yarn
